name: Cambodia

findings.summary: All three main Cambodian mobile operators ran 5G trials on Huawei equipment in 2019, following a government agreement with Huawei signed in April 2019; Smart Axiata awaited spectrum and a licence before launch.
findings.analyst_inference: Trials are tier 2; no source found here confirming commercial 5G RAN/core contracts or vendor shares per operator. Metfone is a Viettel (Vietnam) subsidiary per general knowledge, not verified in these sources.

findings.summary: The Sihanoukville-Hong Kong (SHV-HK) submarine cable, about 2,900 km, built by HMN Tech for China Unicom Global and co-funded by Cambodia's telecoms ministry, completed landing in late July 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 4 (construction complete) rather than 5 because neither source confirms the system is in commercial service. Co-funding share not disclosed.

findings.summary: Cellcard signed an MoU with Huawei reported at US$300 million covering investment in 5G and AI, marking a partnership the article dates to 1999.
findings.analyst_inference: Only the headline and metadata were readable; scope beyond 5G and AI not confirmed. MoU is non-binding (tier 1).

findings.summary: Data-centre firm ByteDC signed an MoU with Huawei Cambodia on hybrid cloud, aiming to become a Huawei public cloud distributor while investing in private cloud infrastructure.
findings.analyst_inference: ByteDC ownership and nationality not stated in source.

findings.local_actor: Royal Government of Cambodia (Prime Minister Hun Manet)
findings.summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet met ZTE executives at WAIC 2026 in Shanghai; both sides agreed to deepen cooperation on 5G deployment, AI applications and ICT talent. No signed documents, projects or values reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Source tiered S4: text appears to relay a ZTE corporate release (same headline appears on ZTE's own site, not fetched). Statement of intent only.

findings.summary: More than 200 surveillance cameras donated by China were switched on in Phnom Penh about five months after installation began. Vendor, value and date not stated in the page read.

sources.publisher: Open Development Cambodia (republishing The Cambodia Daily)

findings.analyst_inference: Donor is the PRC government but the camera vendor and system operator are not named, so the controller pole is unclear; a related headline reports China gave $3m for a city surveillance system (not fetched). Likely late-2010s.

findings.summary: Nasdaq-listed KIDZ AI agreed to take a 2% stake in Phnom Penh's operational Tier III facility, which the government has designated the national cloud data centre, with first refusal on up to 1 MW.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner's ultimate parent jurisdiction is not stated, so pole is null; the company name alone is not evidence of PRC control. Stake value undisclosed; operational status is the company's own claim.

findings.summary: Cambodia's telecoms ministry reported it is developing a Khmer-language large language model built on Meta's open-weight Llama 3, to ease AI adoption including content creation. Still in development as of February 2025.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded domestic because the ministry controls the fine-tuned weights; base model is US-origin open weights (Llama 3), so update/licence dependence on Meta persists.

findings.summary: KIDAI-A, billed as a sovereign Khmer-language AI agent for document processing, locally hosts open-weight models including Qwen, Gemma and GPT-OSS variants; listed as under development with a working prototype.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: mixes PRC (Qwen) and US (Gemma, GPT-OSS) base models, and the developer is not named on the page (source link points to a Techo Startup Center subdomain).

silicon.null_reason: no public accelerator purchases, deployments or licence decisions surfaced in data-centre and AI searches

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced; search budget spent on other layers

research_gaps: Which vendors supply RAN and core for Smart Axiata, Metfone and Cellcard today, and has commercial 5G launched (a 2026 launch was announced; article redirect not fetched)?
Is SHV-HK in commercial service, and what was the ministry's co-funding share?
Ultimate ownership of HUADING DEVELOPMENT (CAMBODIA), operator of the national cloud data centre.
Vendor, date and value of the China-donated Phnom Penh surveillance cameras, and any later safe-city expansion.
Status of the MPTC Khmer LLM and whether government services adopt a foreign frontier model.
No reversals found in one targeted search; a broader check is warranted.
